Click the preview to sample the exact background color — no guessing hex codes.
Feather control softens edges so cutouts look natural, not jagged.

faqs.a: Upload the photo, pick the background color (or click the preview to sample it), choose flood-fill or chroma-key mode, adjust tolerance, and press Download. The background becomes transparent or your chosen color.
faqs.q: How do I remove a photo background?

faqs.a: Flood-fill starts from the image edges and removes only connected background areas — best when the subject touches no border in the background color. Chroma-key removes the color everywhere, including inside the subject.
Click directly on the background in the preview. The tool reads that exact pixel's color and sets it as the target.
faqs.q: How do I pick the exact background color?

faqs.a: Yes. Choose White or a custom color instead of Transparent, and the removed area is filled with it on download.
faqs.q: Can I replace the background with a color instead?

faqs.a: Honestly: it works on solid, even backgrounds (studio backdrops, green screens, white product shots). Busy or gradient backgrounds give messy results — that is a hard limitation of color-keying.
faqs.q: Will it work on any photo?

faqs.a: No. Every pixel is processed with JavaScript in your browser; the photo is never uploaded.

solid-background-remover.formula:
dist = √((r−tr)² + (g−tg)² + (b−tb)²)
remove pixel if dist ≤ tolerance × 2   (tolerance 0–100 → 0–200 units)
feather: alpha ramps from 0 to 1 across the feather band
howTo: Upload the photo with a solid-color background.
Click the background in the preview to sample its exact color, or set it with the color picker.
Choose flood-fill (edges inward) or chroma-key (everywhere) mode.
Adjust tolerance until the background disappears without eating the subject; add feather to soften edges.
Pick transparent, white, or a custom replacement background, then Download.
keyFacts: Color-keying removes pixels whose color is within a tolerance distance of your target color.
Flood-fill mode grows the removal region inward from the image borders.
Tolerance maps 0–100 to a color distance of 0–200 (max possible distance is about 442).
Feather creates a soft alpha ramp at the boundary instead of a hard edge.
The removed-percentage readout tells you exactly how much of the image was keyed out.

limitations: Works only on solid, even-colored backgrounds — not on busy, textured, or gradient scenes.
Fine hair, fur, and semi-transparent edges cannot be separated cleanly by color.
Anti-aliased edges may leave a faint halo of the old background color.
This is color-keying, not AI segmentation: it cannot understand what the subject is.

solid-background-remover.workedExample:
Target color pure green #00FF00 = (0, 255, 0), pixel (10, 240, 10), tolerance 15 (→ 30 distance units):
dist = √(10² + 15² + 10²) = √425 ≈ 20.6
20.6 ≤ 30, so the pixel is removed (alpha → 0).
A subject pixel (200, 50, 60): dist = √(200² + 205² + 60²) ≈ 292.6 > 30, so it is kept fully opaque.
